title: Nymph (immature stage) of an Assassin Bug from the family Reduviidae
Fuzzy Caterpillar
desc: I noticed this caterpillar on my kayak while kayaking on Lake Collins. I then carefully paddled back to camp so that I could take pictures of it. I had to rescue it a few times when it fell into the water.

title: Sabertooth Longhorn Beetle
desc: This bug was about 5 or 6 inches long. Amazon Jungle, Peru

title: Migrant Hawker Dragonfly
desc: This dragonfly was on a totem pole in Ketchikan, Alaska. I started taking pictures of it and suddenly people were more interested in the dragonfly than the totem pole.

title: Dungeness Crab
desc: This crab is waiting for dinner time. Alaska

title: Earwig
desc: I know this just seems wrong, but this earwig was on a cupcake at work and the white icing made a nice background for a photo

title: Two Red Dragonflies
desc: Taken on the boat ride at the beginning of the Milford Track. The heart seemed appropriate.

title: Tarantula
desc: I got to hold this tarantula after running the Brazen Tarantula 5K.

title: Snowman
desc: Not a bug, but I made this little snowman while on a backpacking trip in the Marble Mountains of Northern California. There was snow on the ground in early August. The snowman is about one foot tall.

title: Ostrich
desc: We saw this guy when we visited an ostrich farm in Arizona. The ostriches are big, strong, and scary!

title: Owl Moth
desc: When seen from the top, this moth looks like it has the eyes of an owl. This is one of the first bug pictures I ever took. I had been inspired by a science talk about bugs and flowers, given by a local professor at Feather River Camp.

title: Owl Moth
desc: See how the spots look like the eyes of an owl?

title: Monarch Butterfly
desc: Ready for takeoff! Captain Cook, Hawaii

title: Emu
desc: This picture was taken by a friend while visiting New Zealand.

title: Green Anole
desc: This guy was on the back of our rental car in Hawaii. It's in the iquana family.

title: Gecko
desc: I loved these little guys. They were all over our rented house in Hawaii.

title: Butterflies
desc: These were three of many at a lunch stop while backpacking in the Marble Mountains.

title: King Spider
desc: This spider was in the men's room at the ATV tour in Hawaii. Vincent told me it was there and I ran in to get a picture. The spider was about 8 inches in diameter.

title: Praying Mantis
desc: I was able to take pictures for about 10 minutes before it flew away.

title: Birthday Cake
desc: Jamie made me a birthday cake. One day, after wae had eaten some of it, I opened the refrigerator and this half eaten bear was smiling at me. I love this picture.

title: Jumping Spider
desc: I found this spider in the mailbox one day. I ran in the house and got my camera, then proceeded to coax the spider out of the mailbox where I could get more light. I later found out that it was a JUMPING spider! Luckily, it didn't jump while I was bothering it.

title: Wasp
desc: I believe this is a wasp. It landed on a pack while I was wailing to zipline. Amazon Jungle, Peru.

title: Tail-less Whip Scorpion
desc: Saw this during a night hike in the Amazon jungle, Peru.
